blueprint_profile.description: Reusable security and assurance FR/TBT templates. This pack currently includes versioned mappings to OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 rows; other compliance mappings must be authored as additional versioned mapping packs rather than encoded in the blueprint IDs.

ASVS.reason: Reusable security-core assurance blueprint coverage for common application security obligations.

frs.title: Session timeout and re-authentication
frs.description: The application must reject expired session credentials, expire inactive sessions, require re-authentication after session expiry, update activity timestamps safely, and deny or clean up expired or empty sessions.

applicability.notes: Blueprint applicability must be reviewed against the project SOW/design and implementation before adoption.

frs.title: Contextual output encoding and injection resistance
frs.description: The application must canonicalize input safely and apply context-appropriate output encoding for HTML, XML, URL, JavaScript, JSON, CSS, and HTTP response contexts.

applicability.notes: Blueprint applicability must be reviewed against the project SOW/design and implementation before adoption.

frs.title: Trusted service-layer input validation and business rules
frs.description: The application must document and enforce trusted service-layer validation for expected input formats, contextual consistency, and business logic limits.

applicability.notes: Blueprint applicability must be reviewed against the project SOW/design and implementation before adoption.

frs.title: Browser security headers and cookie protections
frs.description: The application must set secure cookie attributes and browser security response headers that constrain transport, content loading, content sniffing, and client-side exposure.

applicability.notes: Blueprint applicability must be reviewed against the project SOW/design and implementation before adoption.

frs.title: Safe file upload, storage and download handling
frs.description: The application must constrain uploaded files by documented type and size, use safe server-side file names and paths, and scan untrusted files before serving them back to users.

applicability.notes: Blueprint applicability must be reviewed against the project SOW/design and implementation before adoption.

frs.title: Function and data authorization at trusted service boundaries
frs.description: The application must document and enforce function-level, data-specific, and administrative authorization rules at a trusted service layer.

applicability.notes: Blueprint applicability must be reviewed against the project SOW/design and implementation before adoption.

frs.title: Self-contained token integrity and audience validation
frs.description: The application must validate self-contained token signatures, allowed algorithms, token validity windows, and intended audience before accepting token claims.

applicability.notes: Blueprint applicability must be reviewed against the project SOW/design and implementation before adoption.

frs.title: Sensitive data classification, minimization and retention
frs.description: The application must identify sensitive data, avoid leaking it through URLs or excessive responses, apply retention controls, and use anti-cache controls where sensitive data is returned.

applicability.notes: Blueprint applicability must be reviewed against the project SOW/design and implementation before adoption.

frs.title: Dependency inventory and vulnerability remediation
frs.description: The application must maintain an SBOM or dependency inventory and keep third-party components within documented risk-based remediation timeframes.

applicability.notes: Blueprint applicability must be reviewed against the project SOW/design and implementation before adoption.

frs.title: Approved cryptography, key lifecycle and random values
frs.description: The application must maintain cryptographic inventory and use approved cryptographic implementations, algorithms, password hashing, and non-guessable random values.

applicability.notes: Blueprint applicability must be reviewed against the project SOW/design and implementation before adoption.

frs.title: Governed service operation metadata
frs.description: Security-relevant service operations must declare governance metadata that supports auditability, clearance requirements, and permitted agent capabilities.

applicability.notes: This blueprint proves metadata declaration only. It must not be used as runtime authorization allow/deny enforcement evidence.

metadata.asvs_description: Verify that HTTP responses include a Content-Security-Policy response header field which defines directives to ensure the browser only loads and executes trusted content or resources, in order to limit execution of malicious JavaScript. As a minimum, a global policy must be used which includes the directives object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none' and defines either an allowlist or uses nonces or hashes. For an L3 application, a per-response policy with nonces or hashes must be defined.

metadata.asvs_description: Verify that all HTTP responses contain an 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' header field. This instructs browsers not to use content sniffing and MIME type guessing for the given response, and to require the response's Content-Type header field value to match the destination resource. For example, the response to a request for a style is only accepted if the response's Content-Type is 'text/css'. This also enables the use of the Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB) functionality by the browser.
